title: Appending Bits by a Write Action
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $y,x,u$ be Boolean words, let $q,q'\in\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$, and let $p$ be an input-head position among the $|y|+2$ positions. For any input-head movement $m\in\{-1,0,1\}$ and optional bits $b_x,b_u$, applying the action that writes each present bit at its respective buffer head and advances that head exactly when it writes, while moving the input head by $m$, to the loader configuration with buffers $x,u$ and head positions $|x|,|u|$ yields the loader configuration with state index $q'$, buffers $x$ and $u$ extended by $b_x$ and $b_u$, input-head position obtained by the clamped move from $p$, and buffer-head positions equal to the lengths of the extended buffers.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic machine over Booleans
$q,q'$ are in the six-element loader state set
$p$ is a valid input-head position for input $y$
replaced: Let $N$ be a nondeterministic machine and consider a loader configuration whose two buffer heads stand at the right blanks of the buffer words $x$ and $u$. Applying an action that optionally writes one bit at each of the two buffer heads (advancing a head exactly when it writes) produces the loader configuration whose buffers are $x$ and $u$ with the respective optional bits appended, with the physical input head moved by the action's input move and all other tapes unchanged.
